verdict: Alphabet's revenue rose 12% to $90.2B as Search, YouTube and Cloud all grew at double-digit rates — and an $8.0B paper gain on a private-company investment flattered the bottom line, lifting net income 46% to $34.5B.

segments.name: Google Services
segments.note: Search, YouTube, subscriptions and devices. Revenues grew 10%, with Search, subscriptions and YouTube ads all up double digits.

segments.name: Google Cloud
segments.note: Cloud computing for businesses — growth of 28% on AI infrastructure and generative AI tools.

segments.name: Other Bets
segments.note: Moonshot projects like Waymo self-driving cars; they lost $1.2B this quarter.

segments.name: Hedging gains
segments.note: Gains on Alphabet's currency-hedging program, which exists to smooth out exchange-rate swings.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineers and AI research; up 14% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling ads and cloud contracts, and marketing Google's products.

follow100Note: Google Services is $85.63 of every $100 Alphabet takes in; a one-off investment gain added an unusual $12.39 below the operating line. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
otherDetail: A net gain of $11,183M — dominated by a $9,758M gain on equity securities, including an $8.0B unrealized gain on a private-company stake, plus interest income net of interest expense.

takeaways.title: Cloud is compounding
takeaways.text: Google Cloud revenue grew 28% to $12.3B and its operating profit rose to $2.2B from $0.9B a year ago — the AI buildout is turning into real earnings, not just sales.

takeaways.title: A paper gain did heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Other income included an $8.0B unrealized gain on a private-company stake; with related items it added about $7.7B to net income after tax — most of the 46% jump — without anything being sold.

takeaways.title: Over a third of revenue became profit
takeaways.text: Net income hit $34.5B, a 38% margin — but strip out the investment gain and the underlying margin was closer to 30%, still strong.

oneTimers: An $8.0 billion unrealized gain on non-marketable equity securities — Alphabet's stake in a private company — sits in other income. Together with related items it added $7.7B to net income (and $0.62 to EPS) after tax; it is a paper gain, not cash earned by the business.
